symptom: Even after policy-first ordering, the deny-only synthetic claimed-anchor and reference helpers traversed a caller claim before snapshotting proof refs. A claim descriptor or ownKeys Proxy trap could repair an initially mismatching policySnapshotDigest before nested signature math, yielding positive caller-claim consistency for a different entry-time proof reference. This never established independent authority or scoring.
lesson: Policy-first ordering alone does not protect proof references from a later claim Proxy. All related caller-owned graphs that claim traversal could mutate must be pinned before that traversal and reused through nested math and request reconstruction.
guardrail: In synthetic claimed-anchor/reference correlation, detach policy and proof refs before traversing claim; reuse those detached graphs for signature math and all subsequent proof-request builds. Regressions must trigger claim descriptor/ownKeys traps that actually repair original mismatched refs, yet still reject them with literal independentAuthorityVerified=false and scoringAuthorized=false. Keep independent reference pinned first and do not claim atomic cross-input snapshots.
